name: Smoke Point in Co-flow Experiment (SPICE)
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME)
lead_investigators: Peter B. Sunderland (University of Maryland, Principal Investigator)
Richard L. Axelbaum (Washington University in St. Louis)
description: SPICE determined the laminar smoke-point properties of non-buoyant hydrocarbon jet diffusion flames burning under controlled co-flow velocities in microgravity. Without buoyancy to accelerate exhaust gases and narrow flame tips, soot residence times increase dramatically in microgravity, shifting smoke emission thresholds. SPICE measured smoke-point flame lengths and fuel mass flow rates across various nozzle diameters to guide space habitat smoke detector sensitivity and soot emission models.
apparatus: ACME insert in CIR, featuring round brass and stainless-steel fuel nozzles (1.6 mm, 2.1 mm, 2.7 mm inner diameter), laminar co-flow air duct (5 to 40 cm/s), color ratio pyrometry cameras, soot optical transmission laser, and exhaust gas sensors.
